facts.content: Patient has swelling in the left elbow for approximately one week.
facts.source_text: CC: L elbow swelling x ~1 wk

facts.content: The swelling is nonpainful, warm, and feels fluid-filled.
There is no history of trauma and full range of motion.
No prior episodes of elbow swelling.
Patient has a history of osteoarthritis diagnosed years ago by a general practitioner.
facts.source_text: PMH: OA (dx by GP, yrs ago)

facts.content: Patient is not on any medications.
Patient is allergic to peanuts.
Patient has no known drug allergies.
Patient denies family history of rheumatoid arthritis or lupus.
Patient has a desk-based occupation.
Patient runs 2 to 3 times a week and is otherwise well.
Visible swelling over the left olecranon; slightly warm compared to adjacent skin.
facts.source_text: Video exam: visible swelling over L olecranon; slightly warm vs adjacent skin

facts.content: Mild tenderness adjacent to the swelling; tip of olecranon non-tender.
facts.source_text: Tenderness mild adjacent to swelling; olecranon tip non-tender

facts.content: Dry skin noted over the tip of the elbow.
Full range of motion in the elbow.
Left olecranon bursitis considered atraumatic with low concern for septic arthritis.
facts.source_text: L olecranon bursitis—atraumatic, warm, mild focal TTP, preserved ROM; low concern for septic arthritis currently

facts.content: Osteoarthritis history per patient.
Peanut allergy.
Start ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily with food over the counter.
facts.source_text: Start ibuprofen 400 mg BID with food (OTC)

facts.content: Ibuprofen should be discontinued if heartburn occurs.
Send lab forms and obtain inflammatory markers, infection screen, rheumatologic antibodies, and uric acid/gout screen.
facts.source_text: Labs: send forms; obtain inflammatory markers, infection screen, rheumatologic antibodies, uric acid/gout screen

facts.content: Follow up after lab results in approximately 5 to 6 days post-draw via clinic, phone, or video, per patient preference.
facts.source_text: F/U after labs (~5–6 days post-draw) via clinic/phone/video per patient preference

facts.content: Urgent review if the elbow becomes very red, very painful, or if redness spreads due to concern for septic joint.
facts.source_text: Safety-net: urgent review if elbow becomes very red, very painful, or redness spreads (concern for septic joint)
